newsitem.title: USA: Republicans in Congress reassure on wanting tax cuts.
newsitem.headline: Republicans in Congress reassure on wanting tax cuts.

text.p: Republican lawmakers offered reassurances Sunday that the House of Representatives leadership still firmly backed tax cuts, a keystone of the party platform.
"We're not giving up our commitment to tax cuts," said Rep. Tom DeLay, House assistant majority leader, on the "Fox News Sunday" television program.
House Speaker Newt Gingrich last week stirred up a furor among members of his own party with a suggestion that tax cuts should be taken up after a balanced budget deal.
The Republican from Georgia said later his comments had been misunderstood and he was not backing off from seeking tax reductions this year.
DeLay, a Texas Republican, said it was more a tactical maneuver that mimicked success last year in passing a welfare reform bill that President Clinton signed into law.
"When we pulled welfare reform out by itself we passed it ... because we focused the nation on welfare reform, the president had to sign it even though he didn't want to," DeLay said.
"We think we can do the same thing by focusing the country on Medicare by itself, Medicaid by itself and tax cuts by itself, and the nation will force the president to sign it," he said.

"We are not giving any ground at all. We are still committed to balancing the budget and give significant tax cuts," DeLay said. "We're just saying the strategy ought to be different from the strategy that did not get us tax cuts," he added.
Jack Kemp, former Republican vice president candidate, said tax cuts should be done first to allow stronger economic growth and then budget policy should be taken up.
"By putting budget in balance first and tax rate reduction second, we never get to the tax rate reduction," Kemp said on ABC Television's "This Week."

Rep. Bill Paxon, a New York Republican who is part of the House leadership, said on the same program: "We are absolutely committed to inextricably linking balancing the budget and tax relief at the exact same time, no change in that position."
